recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits far below the block threshold and no evidence-based danger window applies, because every published hour falls inside the CME weekend halt and no price path can form. The scheduled 22:00Z Sunday futures reopen falls about eleven hours beyond the final slot in this window. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active as always.
headline: A 3.75-4.00% policy rate, a ten-year on 5% and crude easing to $100.30 wait out the weekend halt behind a 14.81 VIX, with Tail at its floor
body: Every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt. Cash equities closed at 20:00Z on Friday, the E-mini settled near 21:00Z, and equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday - roughly eleven hours after the final slot in this window. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources this hour. The cash Nasdaq-100 settled at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from a 29,447.00 previous close, finishing 3.6 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range; the Nasdaq Composite added 0.39% and the S&P 500 0.17%, while the Dow slipped 0.18%. VIX fell 4.08% to 14.81 and settled at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range. Friday was a quadruple-witching expiry alongside the quarterly rebalance and it cleared without disorder, so the closing strength carried substantial mechanical flow rather than persistent momentum - a reason not to read it as one-way structure. The week's anchor was Wednesday's FOMC decision: a unanimous 12-0 vote raising the target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% with inflation described as elevated, alongside a dot plot in which 16 of 18 participants see at least one further 2026 hike. The ten-year finished Friday at 4.997%, up about six basis points, after topping 5.04% before the decision - its highest since 2007 - with the H.15 two-year at 4.67% at the September 17 observation. Crude eased for a third session, WTI settling $100.30 (-1.58%) and Brent near $104, as the market judged the Saudi East-West pipeline outage less disruptive than first feared; Riyadh has rerouted barrels through Hormuz and is working to restore about half of the line's capacity within days. The unresolved Middle East shipping file remains the clearest conditional route to a weekend gap: Hormuz transit is still heavily restricted and tankers were struck on September 9 and 13. Leadership on Friday was narrow and semiconductor-led, with the SOX up 2.78% and memory names strongest, while megacaps split evenly. None of that can be tested inside this window. Because a halted contract cannot produce shallow pullbacks, failed retracements, repeated extension or session-extreme holding, Tail sits at its structural floor of 5 and rises only to 6 late in the window as untested headline exposure accumulates toward a reopen that still falls outside it. Stress drifts from 22 to 25 on evidence staleness rather than observed difficulty, and Confidence steps down from 76 to 63 for the same reason. Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with no evidence-based danger window applicable. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active as always.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail ran 15-18 through the European morning and the dispersed U.S. cash session, then fell through 16, 11, 7 and 6 as trading ended and the contract settled, holding 5 across the final twelve hours. Stress peaked at 51 during the U.S. afternoon and decayed through 44, 33, 28 and 26 into the halt, reaching 21 across five consecutive slots before ticking to 22. Confidence held between 75 and 88, drifting lower only once the halt removed any refreshing observation. Dominant mode rotated from mixed across the cash session to trend-up into the close, then to normal for the whole post-settlement stretch.
outlookSummary: All 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt: cash closed at 20:00Z on Friday, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z, and CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, about eleven hours after the final slot here. Tail is held at 5 through Saturday and the Sunday small hours, lifting to 6 only from 06:00Z as untested weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of the reopen; that single point reflects proximity and accumulation, never observed structure. Stress drifts from 22 to 25, crossing into the moderate band late on staleness alone. Confidence steps down from 76 to 63 across the window, describing an evidence set ageing without refresh rather than rising danger. Dominant mode is normal throughout, because a closed market cannot express a trend. The identified conditional routes to a gap are the unresolved Middle East shipping and pipeline file, the rates path after a hike that left the ten-year on 5%, and any weekend policy commentary. The Saudi Exchange Sunday session, roughly 07:00-12:00Z, is the only venue able to price the pipeline repair before the window closes.
